answer.rationale: The competitor price cut creates strong pull toward promotional_pricing, but memory_73 is explicit and unusually specific: it lifted acquisition and revenue while materially reducing 30-day retention, with a standing instruction not to generalize it as a growth strategy. Matching a deeper cut against a price-sensitive base that is already churn-prone would likely trade sustainable qualified revenue for a short revenue spike — the opposite of the primary objective. Of the remaining options, only two are backed by source records I actually recovered and re-verified this cycle: exp_86 (onboarding: completion +13%, TTV -2.1d, 30-day retention +3%) and exp_91 (activation messaging: week-one engagement +11%, activation +6%, 30-day retention +1%). Both are confirmed, so I am not relying on unverified summary text. I choose activation_messaging over simplify_onboarding because the acute problem is retention conversations with existing SMB accounts, and in-product activation messaging reaches accounts already in the funnel, whereas onboarding changes only affect new signups and cannot act on this week's churn risk. Onboarding simplification (memory_31/memory_86) remains the right parallel investment for the next cycle. Uncertainty I am deliberately not collapsing: exp_91's retention effect (+1%) was measured absent competitive price pressure, and there is no evidence that engagement lift neutralizes a deep price delta; it may slow churn without stopping it. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) and referral_incentive (memory_57) are plausible but address different segments than the one under attack, and neither was re-verified this cycle. Because my verification budget is exhausted, I am running this as a standard experiment with retention as the primary metric rather than a broad rollout, so the competitive-pressure conditions get measured rather than assumed. Downstream risk flagged: if this cycle's result is consolidated into durable memory, it must be recorded with the competitive-shock context attached, and memory_73's retention caveat must not be quietly dropped by a future session reading only the revenue line.
